verdict.reason:
I could not refute it. I re-checked it on my own and the numbers reproduce.

**Code.** At c2c8b8b, the grid is {3/3, 2/2, 4/5, 5/5} (main.m:89 and train_dqn.m:68). policy_monitor.m:185 confirms an alarm when at least m of the last n cycles carried one. Every monitor in the grid needs two or more consecutive alarm cycles. choose_drop_threshold.m:136-142 combines the confirmations with OR. Today that union equals 2/2. Adding a plain 2/4 would make the union 2/4, so the drop threshold would get stricter for every monitor, as the finding says.

**Physics.** The sweep period is uniform over 20-83.5 ms (init_params.m:255-264) and the dwell lasts 5.25 ms (sweep_window_s.m). Per-cycle presence is therefore periodic, not random.

**My run** (scratchpad/audit1/vfy_loopmon/vfy_mon.m and .log): 368 validation sweeper sub-runs, out-of-fold monitor class, 17-20 cycles after the onset.
- Target share 57.3%, read share 55.7%, 0.57 class changes per cycle.
- The cycles alternate: P(read at t | read at t-1) is 0.37 and P(target at t | target at t-1) is 0.38. Consecutive-cycle rules do worse here than the finding's binomial check suggests.
- Never confirmed by class alone: 11.1% (2/2), 67.7% (3/3), 61.1% (4/5), 76.9% (5/5), 2.7% (2/4).
- With the BER-window degradation added: 5.7 / 12.0 / 10.6 / 19.6%, and 1.6% at 2/4.
- Packet-loss-harmed sub-runs (127): never confirmed at most 1.6% for every monitor. The p90 delay is 7.8 / 9 / 9.9 / 12 cycles, against 3 at 2/4. The finding's "9/10/10/12" is the p90 over all sub-runs, not over the harmed ones; this is a small correction.
- The test set agrees: p1.log:1064 gives 2/2 by class, median 3, p90 12, never 12.7%.

**A new effect I found** (vfy_mon2.m). The no_action escalation (policy_decide.m:110-111, C.esc = 3 consecutive confirmed cycles) exists for "a jammer between our packets". Under class-only 2/2 it never fires in 67.9% of sweeper sub-runs. With class or degradation it never fires in 14.7%.

**Problems with the proposed fix.**
- 3/6 adds almost nothing: by class alone it never confirms in 7.3%, with p90 10 cycles.
- A plain 2/4 raises clean confirmations through non-sweeper misreads. On the 32 clean validation sub-runs at 6 dB and above: by class, 15.6% rises to 25.0%; with degradation, 34.4% rises to 40.6%. C2's false-alarm bound would probably reject it.
- Both rows add 18 DQN runs each to C2, and 2/4 also forces the per-row rework of choose_drop_threshold.m.

The sweeper class, however, is never read on clean validation cycles (0.00%). Outside the WLAN sub-runs (7.5% of them confirmed by sweeper reads, the same at 2/2 and 2/4), no sub-run of another class is confirmed by sweeper reads. So a confirmation path for the gated sweeper alone keeps the full benefit at no false-alarm cost.

**Severity: MAJOR.** No KPI has been measured yet; C2 has not run. But the sweeper is the largest class (20.3% of the frames above the KPI 1 threshold) and has the worst confirmation latency of all classes. The escalation path designed for exactly this threat fails, and the fix has to land before C1d/C2, which have not started (the log is at OOD).

verdict.reason:
Part (1) holds. Part (2) and the v6 evidence do not.

What holds: in policy_decide.m:88-91 (c2c8b8b), any proposal that differs from the stored candidate resets the dwell, and so do no_action and p == cfg. A commit therefore needs C.dwell = 2 identical proposals on consecutive cycles (decision_config.m:29). In v7 the sweeper is intermittent by its physics. p1.log:437 says it is on our channel in 55.8% of decision cycles. The fused class follows the per-cycle targets (D85/D86), so the monitor's class physically alternates between sweeping_jammer and none. The rule then alternates too:
- sweeping_jammer cycles propose freq_diversity (rule_based_policy.m:60-62).
- none cycles on a degraded window propose freq_diversity+power_control, or channel_switch when the quiet slot is hot (rule_based_policy.m:82-91).
- none cycles on a clean window propose no_action.
freq_diversity and freq_diversity+power_control are the same physical answer, yet each switch between them resets the count.

The claimant's validation proxy (val_loop3.m) is a fair open-loop reading: out-of-fold monitor class, the 5-frame BER window, measured mmse_gain and q_iot. Its proposal shares (freq_diversity 53%) match the 55.8% per-cycle presence. It has two flaws:
- At line 46, operator precedence reduces the 2-of-4 test to 'any proposal seen twice'.
- It ignores escalation from no_action.
Under 2/2 confirmation the dwell adds about 4 points of sub-runs with no rule commit (10.9 vs 7.1%). Under 3/3 it adds about 12 points (24.7 vs 12.8%). 3/3 is in the C-stage monitor grid (train_dqn.m:68), and v6 deployed it. Confirmation (shared with the DQN shield) is a separate bottleneck: B3 shows confirmed alarm never in 12.7% (p1.log:1064). The DQN has no dwell. So on intermittent threats (the sweeper and its combos, WLAN, blind_esc) the dwell holds back rule_esc, the KPI 5 baseline (measure_all_kpis.m:265), and rule_sel, the fallback. The table policy is held back the same way. This goes against the project's own D28 rule: a baseline that contradicts the system's physics makes the DQN's advantage artificial. C2 has not run, so the change costs no test reading.

What does not hold:
(a) The v6 numbers are not evidence for the dwell. In v6 the sweeper was read at 99%, so the class did not flicker, and the table had the same dwell yet reached 91.4%. rule_esc made 3.13 changes per sweeper episode on validation (v6 diag_switching.txt), so its deficit came from what it committed, not from failing to commit.
(b) The 'class-blind ladder leaves the sweeper unmitigated' claim does not hold. Ladder steps 1 and 2 both carry spatial_diversity+power_control. MMSE nulls a single directional sweeper. channel_switch adds nothing against the sweeper (D28), so in the fixed configuration channel_switch+spatial_diversity+power_control the spatial nulling and power do the work. That configuration restored 91.4% of v6 test sweeper episodes, equal to the table, the best non-DQN policy. Fix part (2) is not evidenced and could replace an effective step.
(c) Fix (1) as written creates a ping-pong. With cfg = freq_diversity, the degraded-none cycles propose freq_diversity+power_control, which shares the element, so it commits. The next sweeper cycles then propose freq_diversity, which commits back. That repeats every hold period.

The closed-loop size is unmeasured, because v7 has no policy pools yet. I did not run MATLAB: commit charge was 94-99 of 101.8 GB with 0.6-1.2 GB of physical RAM free, and the run chain is still going.
verdict.better_fix:
Changes to policy_decide.m, rule and table branches only. No change to the DQN or the monitor.

1. Dwell as m-of-n on proposal groups (Barajas et al. M-of-N, the alarm's existing source). Keep the last 4 proposals in mem.ph (NE x 4) and drop the reset on no_action. Group a proposal by its threat-specific element (freq_diversity, channel_switch, fec_interleave, spatial_diversity); link-budget configurations form their own group, compared on the budget match. Commit the latest proposal when its group appears in >= C.dwell of the 4 entries, under M.confirmed and C.hold as now. A steady proposal gives today's behaviour.

2. No-regress guard, needed to avoid the ping-pong. When the configuration in use already contains the proposal's threat-specific element, treat the proposal as satisfied and do not change. Change only when the proposal adds an element the configuration lacks. Also skip proposals that are already in mem.tried during the incident (mem.tried is cleared after C.heal healthy cycles). Without this, the rule re-commits a configuration the escalation has just left because it failed.

3. Leave C.ladder unchanged: its steps 1-2 contain spatial_diversity+power_control, which nulls a single sweeper. If a class-informed first escalation step is wanted, add it as a variant chosen on validation only, never by default.

4. Before C2, measure on validation for rule_esc, rule_sel and table on both profiles:
   - recovered %, per threat, with intermittent threats reported separately;
   - changes per episode and A->B->A ping-pong rate (diag_switching.m);
   - the clean-link false-change rate under the KPI 6 bound (the d84_dec.md A1 table: 2-of-4 is looser than 2 consecutive on the drop path's budget flips).
   Adopt only if recovery rises and the false-change bound still holds. The DQN is unaffected. Record the design in DECISIONS.md.

verdict.reason:
I confirmed the finding from the code at c2c8b8b and from saved results. One line reference is wrong and one sub-claim is weaker than stated.

Mechanism (confirmed):
- `link_env.m:157-174` loops `a = 1:nA`, and that loop includes `K.na` (no_action). So `recoverable = any(restored & restored_plr)` is true for any geometry that no_action already restores.
- Per-cycle `restored` comes from the per-geometry mean tables (`link_env.m:262-268`). On a geometry the threat does not harm, no_action is therefore ok on every cycle after the onset.
- `rollout_policy.m:84-92` then gives `t_rec = 0` and `recovered = true`.
- The 'no response' policy is `fixed na` (`policy_setup.m:14`). Its 'recovered' column is therefore exactly the unharmed share of the KPI 4 pool.
- Correction: `rollout_policy.m:162-163` does not exist. The file has 117 lines at c2c8b8b; the relevant lines are 84-92 and 103-104.

Evidence:
- v6 test, `uav-gcs-v6/results/policy_evaluation.txt` lines 139 and 143: no response 'recovers' 77.5% of the recoverable antenna_fault episodes, 61.1% of airframe_shadowing and 19.7% of benign interference.
- The deployed policy's rate on harmed episodes is bounded only from below: at least (98.1-77.5)/22.5 = 91.6% for antenna_fault and at least 93.3% for shadowing. In v6 the verdict would not flip, but the margin and the sample shrink sharply (about 160 harmed episodes of 720).
- For antenna_fault, 90% overall needs only about 56% of the harmed episodes.
- The envelope (`evaluate_policies.m:266-275`) and KPI 8 (`measure_all_kpis.m:361-363`, `pt >= 50`) share this pool. Any (threat, level) where no response already restores 90% is 'in' without the policy doing anything. No response alone would also meet KPI 8.

Edge map (the strongest part, confirmed):
- DECISIONS.md:733 says the random policy's PROT marks points 'not attributable ... (r; a threat that seldom harms the link)'.
- The random policy picks uniformly every cycle (`policy_decide.m:97-98`), so its held recovery is close to zero whatever the threat does.
- The v7-code smoke run shows this: `uav-gcs-v7-merge/results/edge_summary.txt:160` gives held recovery of 2.4% for random against 26.8% for no response. The 'r' mark can therefore never fire.
- The edge map already computes HM, the flights no_action does not restore (`edge_map.m:192-196`). It also already flies no response at the first delay (lines 165 and 851). Yet PROT, REC and the attribution check ignore both.

Weaker than stated:
- Fault and shadowing get the same response (`rule_based_policy.m:69-70`, power_control). So misattributing one as the other does not by itself change recovery.
- What KPI 4 can hide is a failure of lost-branch detection or response on the harmed episodes. DET_h covers detection only, not the response.
- The v7 size of the effect is unknown. Profile 1 has not reached the C stages yet; the v7 evidence so far is a smoke run (shadowing no response 40% of 20 episodes).
- I did not rerun the v6 pools. Only 2.8 GB of RAM was free while the chain is running, and the test-split result already settles the mechanism.

Severity: MAJOR rather than MINOR. KPI 4 is the main decision-layer KPI. The envelope is fixed on validation in C2e, so its definition must be settled before profile 1 reaches C2e. The edge map's only attribution guard fails at the job DECISIONS.md:733 gives it.
verdict.better_fix:
Fix this without changing `rollout_policy.m`.

1. **`evaluate_policies.m`**
   - Compute harmed per episode from the tables: `ih = sub2ind(size(K.restored), R.scn, R.s, K.na*ones(size(R.s)), R.split, R.r); harmed = ~(K.restored(ih) & K.restored_plr(ih));`.
   - On the test sets, this equals `~RES{si,col('none')}.recovered` (same episodes and frame draws; no response is `fixed na`). Use that as a consistency check.
   - Next to `PT`/`PTsev`, report recovered among the harmed recoverable episodes per threat and severity, with `boot_cluster` intervals. Print the harmed count beside each value.
   - Envelope: compute `ENVv_h` from RV, the validation episodes, the same way. Fix it in C2e before the test is read. A cell where no response alone recovers at least `ENV_MIN` of the validation episodes is marked 'link unharmed' and is not credited to the policy.
   - Pass `KP.per_threat_h`, `KP.per_threat_h_ci`, `KP.n_harmed` and `KP.envelope_h` on to the KPI stage.

2. **`measure_all_kpis.m`**
   - Print the harmed KPI 4 reading as the stricter reading beside the proposal's wording, the same way KPI 1 already does. The status of the proposal's reading stays as worded.
   - KPI 8 counts threats at or above 50% among harmed episodes, or else requires the paired gain over no response for that threat to be above 0.

3. **`edge_map.m`**
   - Use the existing `HM` (line 196) to add PROT_h and REC_h on harmed flights at each point. Below 36 harmed flights, say so instead of giving a verdict.
   - Add a no-response attribution mark beside 'r'. The 'none' policy already runs at `DLY(1)` (lines 165 and 851). Take its PROT verdict per point, `edge_verdict` on `held_k` of its variant, and mark points where it is COMMITTED as not attributable to the decision layer (for example 'n').
   - Count these in `commit_not_attributable`.

4. **Logging.** These are reporting additions only: no pool rebuild, no change to any verdict rule. Log them in DECISIONS.md with the new `edge_map.m` hash before profile 1's C2e and EDGE read the test. Profile 3 gets the same changes.

verdict.reason:
The code facts check out at c2c8b8b. dqn_train_run.m:71-73 scores each checkpoint as dqn_recovered(Re) + 1e-3*mean(Re.ret), and the return only breaks ties. dqn_recovered.m reads R.recovered, meaning any 5-cycle restored run. In train_dqn.m, rule_rec (163), kmin from weakest_threat (179, 398-410, which reads V.recovered), the run selection (193-205), the gate (222) and choose_deployed's rule_sel (225, choose_deployed.m:16, max over rule_rec) all use the transient 'recovered'. R.held is computed in the same rollouts and reaches V through dqn_eval_batches, but nothing in C2 reads it. edge_map.m commits REC and PROT on held (lines 53-56, 347, 559; DECISIONS.md:732).

The mechanism is real in v7's own model, not only in the random-policy anecdote:
(a) A follower with fdelay = 5 (C.fdelay = [0 5], used in training and validation) leaves exactly 5 clean cycles after each hop (link_env.m:279, t - hop_live >= fdelay). A hop-only configuration therefore scores 'recovered' while it is re-acquired every ~7 cycles. That is held = false (nb >= 2).
(b) Escalating into FEC after a recovery opens the decode gap (Q-1 frames not restored, link_env.m step_env), which breaks held. D64 measured that 61-90% of escalations left an already-restoring configuration.
The random-policy figures quoted in the finding are correct (v6 policy_evaluation.txt:10 76.0%, :24 82.8%; DECISIONS.md:732 80.7% / 96.2% for v4).

Why MINOR and not MAJOR:
- No reported number is biased. EDGE reads held honestly, and the selection stays on validation. The cost is that C2 optimizes a proxy instead of the committed metric, so the deployed agent may be suboptimal for PROT.
- The size of the effect is unmeasured. The finding gives no held-vs-recovered figures for trained agents. v6's aggregates suggest the gap is small: DQN+esc single, recovered 96.4%, ok-share 78.1%, median T_rec 4 of about 23.5 post-onset cycles. 0.964 x (1 - 4/23.5) is about 0.80, which fits mostly-held recoveries. The runs differ by about 1 point, comparable to the seed spread (v6 dqn_training.txt: 96.3-97.5%). The DQN beats rule+escalation by 16-19 points on validation, so a held-based gate is unlikely to flip.
- I could not measure this in MATLAB. The machine is at a commit charge of 94.4 of 101.8 GB with 0.5 GB available, while the p1/p3 chains and other analyses run, so starting another process would have put the running chain at risk.

One citation is wrong: held is at rollout_policy.m:93-102 at c2c8b8b, not 152-161.

The fix is cheap and correct, and it is free if applied before C2. C2 has not started (p1.log is at OOD), so no reading is affected.

where: code/detection/compare_architectures.m:59 (templateKernel('Learner','svm') with the default KernelScale of 1); :64 with macro_present :84-88 (the 'beyond' column)
title: The kernel-SVM baseline failed to fit, and the 'beyond' column is a one-class macro-F1
evidence: p1.log:1105: SVM macro-F1 19.82%. Per class: noise_burst 0.0%, antenna_fault 0.0%, WLAN 0.1%, sweeper 0.1%, shadowing 0.1%. On 23 z-scored features, a Gaussian kernel of scale 1 decays to about e^-46 between typical points, so the random-feature SVM cannot generalise and predicts almost everything as one class. The 'beyond' column holds only 'none' frames (p1.log:1032: none 1258). Its macro-F1 is therefore that one class's F1: the near-constant SVM scores 99.7% and the RF 95.1%, against 21.0% for the hybrid.
fix: Use KernelScale 'auto', or the LIBSVM default gamma = 1/p (Hsu, Chang & Lin), with Lambda chosen on validation. Report the beyond-range column as the share read right, as eval_detector.m does, not as a macro-F1.
when: Before the B3a table enters the report, both profiles; together with out-b3a-arch.

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute this finding and could not. Both parts hold.

(1) The SVM baseline did not fit because of its kernel scale.
- compare_architectures.m:59 at c2c8b8b calls templateKernel('Learner','svm') and sets no KernelScale.
- In MATLAB R2026a, KernelParams.m:564-565 sets KernelScale = 1 when none is given.
- featureMapper.m:133 builds the random features as X*W*sqrt(2)/sigma with W~N(0,1). That approximates the kernel exp(-||x-y||^2/sigma^2).
- I measured the 23 z-scored training features of p1 (81312 frames). The median squared distance between random pairs is 39.7 (p10 11.0, p90 89.9). At scale 1 the kernel is about e^-40 between typical points. The finding's e^-46 is the right order.

I reran the same fitcecoc/templateKernel call on a private copy of splits.mat. I read the validation split with frame labels, not the test set, with rng(42). Script and log are in scratchpad\audit1\svmver\ (svm_check.m, svm_check.log).
- KernelScale 1: accuracy 55.44%, macro-F1 20.32%. It predicts 'none' for 95% of frames, and noise_burst, antenna_fault, WLAN, sweeper and shadowing get F1 0.0. This matches p1.log:1105 (55.27% / 19.82%).
- KernelScale 'auto' (the heuristic chose 4.07): accuracy 84.79%, macro-F1 75.82%.
- KernelScale sqrt(23) = 4.80, the LIBSVM default gamma = 1/p in MATLAB's form: accuracy 87.02%, macro-F1 79.68%.

So the 19.8% row is a fitting failure, not a result of the SVM method. The same code gave 69.6% in v4 (PROJECT_LOG.md:830).

(2) The 'beyond' column is a one-class number.
- kpi_ebno.m judges path_loss frames at the configured Eb/N0, which is on the grid. Only frames that are not path_loss and are received below the grid get a NaN bin, and these exist only after a path-loss step, so they are 'none'. p1.log:1032 lists only none (1258 frames).
- macro_present (:84-88) then returns the F1 of 'none' alone. Precision is 1 by construction, so the value is 2r/(1+r), where r is the share read right.
- The hybrid's 21.0% is really 11.7% read right. The SVM's 99.7% comes from predicting 'none' almost everywhere. eval_detector.m:200-210 reports the same frames as 'read right %', so the two outputs use different measures.

Severity MINOR: neither error touches a KPI or the deployed detector. Both would be wrong as printed in a report table. The hybrid already loses to the random forest in this table, so the broken SVM does not change the ranking.
verdict.better_fix:
1. In compare_architectures.m:59, give the kernel an explicit scale: templateKernel('Learner','svm','KernelScale',sqrt(p)), where p = size(feats,2). This is the LIBSVM default gamma = 1/p (Chang & Lin; Hsu, Chang & Lin, 'A Practical Guide to Support Vector Classification'). It is written as sqrt(p) because MATLAB's kernel is exp(-||x-y||^2/s^2) (featureMapper.m:133). On p1 validation it gives macro-F1 79.7%, against 75.8% for 'auto' and 20.3% for the current default.
2. If the baseline is tuned, follow Hsu-Chang-Lin and the project rule: choose KernelScale and Lambda by a small grid on the validation split only, e.g. s in sqrt(p)*2.^(-2:2) and Lambda in 1/n*10.^(-1:2). Then update the header comment at :13, which says 'default settings, no tuning'.
3. Remove the 'beyond' column from the macro-F1 table. Print it as 'beyond range: n frames (none), read right X%' per variant, using 100*mean(yp(m)==yt(m)) as eval_detector.m:205 does. If it stays in the table, label it as one-class recall.
4. Rerun B3a for both profiles on the next fresh test set (B3m) together with out-b3a-arch. Do not reuse the second test set already read. Rerunning the baseline takes about 3 min of SVM fit per profile.

title: Profile 3's real MMSE receiver under a jammer is worse with 4 antennas than profile 1's with 3, and this is not documented
evidence: Under the 10 dB jammer the 4-antenna real receiver loses +8.61 dB to the ideal one, with BER 7.75e-3 / 6.22e-3 at 8 / 10 dB. With 3 antennas the loss is +4.92 dB (4.76e-3 / 3.20e-3). Likely cause: the antennas-alone path weighs with the signal-present (MPDR) covariance of a 32-symbol window. Its loss against MVDR grows with (N-1)·SINR_out/K (Besson 2021, eqs. 22-23), so it is larger with 4 antennas and at high Eb/N0, which matches the floor. DECISIONS.md reports only profile 1's V11. fix: Repeat the D75-style decomposition at n_rx = 4: genie timing and frequency vs estimated, and dd_mvdr with the signal-free residual covariance (as the space-time path uses since D77) or with loading at the thermal floor. when: Before profile 3's C1p (its MMSE configurations' frames) and before profile 3's PHY validation table enters the report.

verdict.reason:
The observation is real, but the finding blames the wrong stage of the receiver.

What holds:
- The log numbers are correct. p3.log:40 has V11 V8b MMSE 4 ant: loss +8.61 dB, BER 7.75e-3 / 6.22e-3 at 8 / 10 dB. p1.log:54 has the 3-antenna row: +4.92 dB, 4.76e-3 / 3.20e-3. The ideal V8b at 10 dB is 4.99e-7 with 4 antennas against 9.99e-6 with 3.
- The 4-antenna real receiver is worse from 4 dB up.
- The same inversion shows in p3's V12c 'flat BER' rows under the 16 dB jammer (p3.log, A4v report). Profile 3 floors at 1.07-1.18e-2 at 12-15 dB; profile 1 at 0.86-0.91e-2.
- DECISIONS.md (lines 658, 811, 902, 971, 1051) reports V11 only for profile 1. Nothing explains profile 3's row.

What is refuted: the cause the finding names. I ran two MATLAB Monte Carlo checks on a private copy (scratchpad audit1/v11/mpdr_check.m and mpdr_check2.m). The model is a flat channel, a 10 dB noise jammer at 42.4 deg with K 10 dB, our signal K 10 dB, rho 0.3, the real spacings (3 ant at 4.80 wl, 4 ant at 3.20 wl), and 32-symbol windows.

1. dd_mvdr exactly as coded (leave-one-out LS channel, covariance of the received samples), started from correct symbols, has no ceiling. 4 antennas beat 3:
   - 6 dB: 1.15e-4 vs 3.06e-4
   - 8 dB: 8.6e-6 vs 2.7e-5
   - It stays within about 1 dB of the clairvoyant combiner.
   The reason: weights trained on the same window's symbols are the LS/DMI reference-signal combiner, so Besson eq. 22's MPDR penalty does not apply.
2. Besson eq. 22's ceiling of about (K-N+2)/(N-1) does appear when the steering vector comes from outside the window (case C, true h). There 4 antennas are worse than 3: 2.37e-3 vs 1.33e-3 at 10 dB.
3. In the code, that case is the flat MMSE first pass, build_threat_model.m:1383-1412. It whitens with the covariance of the window plus 30 symbols either side, which includes our signal. It takes the channel from the training and 4-8 pilots in the whitened domain. That is MPDR with a mismatched steering vector.
4. I reproduced that chain (first pass, then 4 dd_mvdr passes). It gives the real receiver's pattern:
   - First pass at 10 dB: 5.49e-2 (4 ant) vs 3.25e-2 (3 ant).
   - After the dd_mvdr passes: 8.07e-4 vs 3.83e-4, about 2x, the same ratio as V11's 6.22e-3 / 3.20e-3. The inversion starts at about 2 dB.
   - Decision-directed passes cannot repair windows the first pass started wrong.
   - Swapping in the signal-free residual covariance in dd_mvdr, as the finding proposes, makes it worse: 1.63e-3 vs 8.07e-4 at 10 dB with 4 antennas. Decision errors then enter the covariance, which is the reason the code's comment gives for its choice.

Impact is limited, so MINOR is the right severity:
- V11 has no pass/fail limit.
- The run always uses the delay line (init_params.m:66, tdl = true), so its MMSE receiver is the space-time one (rx_taps nt = 9). Its first pass, st_first, already uses a covariance free of our signal (D77).
- In p3's delay-line rows 4 antennas beat 3 (V12c 16 dB, rho 0.3, 64 ns at 9 dB: 9.89e-6 vs 1.68e-4).
- The flat first pass and dd_mvdr reach the run only as the antennas-alone option each frame can pick by pilot error (build_threat_model.m:1524-1528).

I did not run the real receiver's own timing and frequency decomposition at n_rx = 4. Timing pulled off by the jammer (D75's note) may add to the absolute floor; it does not change these conclusions.
verdict.better_fix:
1. Leave dd_mvdr as it is. Its decision-trained LS weights show no ceiling, and the residual-covariance version is worse when the passes start from imperfect decisions.

2. Document profile 3's V11 V8b row now, beside profile 1's in DECISIONS and the report's PHY table:
   - Label the row as the flat receiver. The run deploys the delay-line receiver, whose verdict is V12c's jam rows, and there 4 antennas beat 3.
   - Give the measured cause: the flat MMSE first pass (build_threat_model.m:1383-1412) weighs with a covariance that contains our signal and a channel taken from 4-8 pilots. That is MPDR with steering mismatch. Its loss grows with SNR and with N (Besson 2021, eq. 22-23; Boroson, cited there), and the decision-directed passes keep the windows it started wrong.
   - Also correct the 'MVDR' label in DECISIONS.md:657 to Besson's terms.

3. As a dev check only, try a first pass with a covariance free of our signal and a channel from the known symbols, as st_first does since D77. Candidates:
   - the quiet-slot covariance Rq0, already computed in the receiver, loaded at the noise floor s2;
   - the residual of the training and pilots.
   Test it on V11 V8b and the V12c flat rows of both profiles. Also run a short genie-timing/frequency run at n_rx = 4 to separate any timing share.

4. Adopt that change only in a full rerun of both profiles from A4v. Profile 3's A5 dataset was already generated with the current antennas-alone option, so changing the receiver before profile 3's C1p alone would make C1p inconsistent with A5.

The fusion also adds the idle-time record, which the per-frame network never sees. verdict.reason:
Half of this finding holds up and half does not.

What holds (checked in the code at c2c8b8b and on a private copy of results/detector_predictions.mat):
1. No continuous threat ever ends. run_dataset_sweep.m:166/251 builds each 20-frame sub-run with the threat on from frame 1, or from the onset for path loss, antenna fault and shadowing, until the end. On the second test set, the sub-runs of jamming, noise burst, reactive jamming, spoofing and tone (192 each) contain 0 'none' targets. The closed loop has the same gap: link_env.m (header) runs "clean link until the onset cycle, then the cell's threat" with no end. evaluate_policies never ends a threat. The only place a threat ends is the 3D demo (v3d_engine.m:106 clearThreat), and that is never evaluated. So nothing measures how fast the decision returns to none after a threat stops, or what holding a countermeasure afterwards costs.
2. The only releases ever tested are the gated threats. I reproduced the finding's 99.4%: on the sweeper's off cycles the fused class is none in 99.4% (14 488 cycles), and in 99.4% / 99.7% / 99.9% at 1 / 2 / 3 cycles after the last hit. Sweep gaps are never longer than 3 cycles. D81 added the current frame's own columns, which drive that fast release. A continuous class was never fitted on a window full of threat with a clean current cycle.
3. The A5 counts are right (p1.log:542-543): sweeper 6037 vs 24871 of 46368 frames, WLAN 5610 vs 9510 of 10080. The per-frame and fused readings do use different labels (eval_detector.m:52-56 vs 62-63).

What does not hold:
- Nothing in the code, docs or exports presents 81.17% -> 93.04% as the fusion's gain. metrics.per_frame (eval_detector.m:448) has no consumer, and both lines name their label rule. The label split is the D86 decision (docs/d86_det.md item 1), which is excluded from findings.
- The memory's share is already measured on identical targets. In B2F (p1.log:698-714) the N = 1 fusion scores 90.81% out-of-fold macro-F1 and N = 12 scores 93.32%, so the 12-cycle memory adds about 2.5 points. The rest comes from the label change and the extra inputs. So the decomposition is a wording note for the report, not a defect.

Why MINOR:
- The lingering is bounded by construction. After 12 cycles (240 ms) neither the fusion window nor the 10-frame link-feature window (link_features.m: plr, var_rssi) holds anything from before the offset.
- No KPI reads offsets.
- The open risks are still real: the release time, transient misreads after the end (for example path_loss from the SINR rise via the stp cues), and countermeasure cost and false switches after a threat ends are never charged.

Flaw in the proposed fix: an offset drawn at frames 2-11 of a 20-frame sub-run gives the threat only 1-10 cycles before it ends, so the 12-cycle window is never full and the worst case is not measured. It also leaves as few as 9 cycles after the offset, which censors the 12-cycle flush.
verdict.better_fix:
(1) Report wording, not code: never quote 81.17% vs 93.04% as the fusion's gain. Quote the memory's share from B2F on the same targets (N = 1 90.81% -> N = 12 93.32% out-of-fold, p1.log:698-714). If a split is wanted, add one line beside eval_detector.m:56 and select_fusion.m:72: the per-frame network's argmax scored on the per-cycle targets (macro_f1(y, y1)). That separates the label change from the fusion. An ablation without the idle columns at the chosen N is optional, on the same validation folds only.

(2) Detector offsets (B3m, plus a share in validation so any remedy is chosen there):
- Add a time gate (an end time) on the threat component in build_threat_model.m. Today only the gated jammers have their own timing, and nothing can switch a threat off.

verdict.reason:
I confirmed the logic gap in the code at c2c8b8b, but no run so far has come close to triggering it.

**What the code does.**
- train_dqn.m:221-222 builds the gate against `bsel`, which is the rule + escalation baseline at the DQN's own monitor and drop setting. The test is `gate = vrec(best) >= bsel.rule_rec && fa_ok(best)`.
- choose_deployed.m:14-16 then picks `ir`, the best pooled recovery among the rule settings whose one-sided 95% bound is <= 5%.
- choose_deployed.m:17 deploys 'dqn_esc' whenever `gate` is true, without ever comparing `vrec(best)` with `rule_rec(ir)`.
- So if an admissible rule at another monitor recovers more than the DQN, and the DQN still beats the rule at its own monitor, the policy that is worse on validation gets deployed. The project rule says every selection is made on validation.

**Why it does not matter in practice.**
- Across every earlier full C2 report, the DQN beats rule + escalation by 16-35 points:
  - v6 p1: DQN 96.3-97.5% against the rule's 77.8% (3/3) and 80.9% (2/2).
  - v6 p2: 94.1% against 61.0% and 64.4%.
  - v4/v7 archive: 96.5-98.0% against 71.3%.
- Changing the monitor moves the rule by at most 3.4 points.
- The rule settings measured so far had false-alarm rates of 25-37%, so none of them was admissible anyway.
- C2 has not run yet in v7 (p1.log and p3.log stop at B3/B4-stage output).
- The case needs a rule that both meets the false-alarm bound and recovers more than the DQN. Nothing seen so far suggests that can happen with the 4/5 and 5/5 monitors added in v7.
- The same-monitor comparison is also on purpose for KPI 5 (DECISIONS.md:715, "KPI 5 keeps the same-monitor comparison"; D667 gives the proposal's gate as pooled recovery >= rule).

So this is a consistency gap in the deployment choice, not a measured fault. MINOR is right.

**On the proposed fix.** The weakest-threat condition should not go into the gate:
- The proposal's gate is pooled recovery, and the `base` struct does not compute the rule's per-threat recovery.
- Mixing a weakest-threat test into a pooled comparison could deploy a rule that is worse pooled. That just swaps one inconsistency for another.
verdict.better_fix:
Keep the gate and KPI 5 on the same monitor (bsel), as DECISIONS.md:715 and the proposal define them. Fix only the deployment choice:
- Pass the DQN's pooled validation recovery `vrec(best)` into choose_deployed.
- After computing `ir`, deploy 'dqn_esc' only when the gate passes and either:
  - `rule_up(ir) > bound`, meaning no rule setting is admissible (keep today's lowest-bound branch for that case), or
  - `dqn_rec >= rule_rec(ir)`.
- In code: `if (gate && (rule_up(ir) > bound || dqn_rec >= rule_rec(ir))) || (rule_up(ir) > bound && dqn_up <= rule_up(ir))`.
- Print a second line in dqn_training.txt: the DQN recovery against rule_sel's recovery, plus which of the two was deployed.
- Add one case to the choose_deployed unit test in test_core.m: gate true, admissible `rule_rec(ir)` > `dqn_rec` → expect 'rule_sel'.

Leave the weakest-threat criterion out of the gate. It is reported for KPI 4 and is not part of the proposal's gate. Do this before C2 on profiles 1 and 3. It changes the result only if the edge case actually occurs.

verdict.reason:
I confirmed the finding in the code at c2c8b8b. All the cited lines are correct.

**What the code does**
- `rule_based_policy.m:53` sets sep = mmse_gain_db >= C.rule_mmse_db. That value is a fixed 6 dB in `decision_config.m:32`.
- No source in DECISIONS.md or in git history backs the 6 dB. DECISIONS.md:488 only states it.
- The base loop in `train_dqn.m` (lines 155-165) scores rule_esc only at the hard-coded 6 dB with the slot branch on. It varies only the alarm and drop settings.
- That rule is the gate reference (`train_dqn.m:222`), the fallback that `choose_deployed` picks, and the KPI 5 reference: `evaluate_policies` runs 'rule' and 'rule_esc' on the DQN's monitor.
- The DQN has mmse_gain in its state, so it learns its own threshold. The rule gets less tuning than the DQN, which is unequal.

**The threshold does matter.** I measured mmse_gain on private copies of the profile 1 split (`splits.mat` validation, 20,328 frames). 6 dB sits inside the bulk of the distributions:

| Class | Frames in [3, 6) dB | Frames at 6 dB or more |
|---|---|---|
| jamming | 28.0% | 15.4% |
| noise_burst | 26.9% | 8.9% |
| spoofing | 19.8% | 15.2% |
| reactive_jamming | 26.2% | 16.2% |

- So the constant decides whether the rule nulls in a large share of the frames of four hostile classes.
- The rule reads the gain of a single frame. When the threshold sits in the bulk, the proposal flips from one cycle to the next. Each flip resets the 2-cycle dwell (`policy_decide.m:91`). The threshold therefore changes timing as well as the action, and only an episode-level reading can settle it.

**What does not hold up**
- q_thr itself is sourced. Kazim et al. 2026, eq. 1.3, gives μ ± 3σ ± 2 dB on interference-free samples, and the source text confirms it. 0.10 + 3 × 0.67 + 2 = 4.11 dB, which matches `p1.log:718`.
- The slot test separates the classes cleanly on validation: q_iot ≥ 4.10 dB in 0% of clean, path-loss, fault and shadowing frames, and in 86-100% of jamming, noise-burst, spoofing and tone frames. The slot branch is physically grounded (Xu et al. 2005).
- Its only plausible harm is narrow: a sweeper the detector missed, caught in a dwell (12% of sweeper frames), would get channel_switch instead of freq_diversity.

**Severity: MINOR.** C2 has not run, so the effect on recovery is unmeasured. Escalation already moves to spatial_diversity+power_control after 3 degraded cycles (C.esc = 3), which limits the cost of a missed null to a few cycles.

**Flaws in the proposed fix**
1. Setting q_thr = Inf does not switch off only the D5 branch. It also removes the ~slot guard of the drop branch at `rule_based_policy.m:78`. A drop alarm with interference in the slot would then go to power_control or budget_match instead of the interference rule, and the comparison would be confounded.
2. The fix does not say how the chosen values reach the stages that read the rule at test time. Without that, the rule run at test would differ from the one chosen on validation.

1. Make the two settings explicit inputs:
   - Add the PP fields rule_mmse_db (default C.rule_mmse_db) and rule_slot (default true).
   - In `policy_decide.m` (around line 76), pass them into `rule_based_policy` as arguments.
   - In `rule_based_policy.m`, gate only lines 85-87 with rule_slot. Keep `slot` in the drop-branch guard at line 78 unchanged. Do not touch PP.q_thr; it is part of det_id.
2. Derive the nulling threshold from data instead of leaving 6 dB unsourced:
   - Use the same recipe as q_thr (Kazim et al. 2026, eq. 1.3), applied to mmse_gain on the clean validation frames, where no interferer exists and the predicted gain is only estimation noise.
   - Profile 1: mean 0.73, std 1.18 dB. μ + 3σ = 4.3 dB; with Kazim's 2 dB margin, 6.3 dB.
   - Compute it in `select_fusion.m` next to q_thr and save it in `fusion.mat`.
   - Candidates: {μ+3σ, μ+3σ+2, 3, 9} dB, with rule_slot on and off.
3. Score the candidates in `train_dqn.m`'s base loop (lines 155-165), on validation episodes and the clean validation geometries only. Pick with the existing recovery and false-alarm bound rule:
   - the fallback (rule_sel) at its own monitor;
   - the KPI 5 rule at the DQN's selected monitor.
   The gate at line 222 then compares against the best-tuned rule, which is the conservative direction.
4. Carry the chosen values everywhere the rule is run:
   - Store them in `trained_dqn.mat` (rule_sel.rule_mmse_db, rule_sel.rule_slot, and a rule_cfg for the KPI 5 rule).
   - Make `policy_setup.m`/`evaluate_policies.m`, `edge_map.m`, `measure_latency.m`, the experiments and the GUI set PP from them.
